messages.author: 189f142eeb20e322
messages.subject: Sending commands in insert mode
parts:
First of all, thanks for the plugin. I've been using it for the past few months, and it's been really helpful!

A issue that I'm having after installing NVim-r is that I cannot send commands in insert mode anymore. Is there a way to set it up?

Thanks!

messages.author: b256a2742aacd200
messages.subject: Re: Sending commands in insert mode
parts:
If you want to enable commands in Insert mode, add the following to your vimrc:

let R_insert_mode_cmds = 1

messages.author: 189f142eeb20e322
messages.subject: Re: Sending commands in insert mode
parts:
Thanks a lot!! That worked perfectly!!

I would only like to report a strange thing. I had a problem with '_' changing to '<-', so I added the following line to vimrc:

let R_assign_map = 0

However this was changing every "0" to "<-". Zero was being interpreted as a character. To solve the problem I added the following line to vimrc:

let R_assingn_map = "^" 

That was an uggly solution, but it worked. But it only worked because I don't use "^" in my code.

If I may, I would only suggest that NvimR don't make this assignment for default.

Thanks again!

messages.author: b256a2742aacd200
messages.subject: Re: Sending commands in insert mode
parts:
When you do

let R_assign_map = 0

Nvim-R understands that you want to convert "0" into " <- ". To disable the assign map, you should put in your vimrc:

let R_assign = 0
